tool.name: SunShading
tool.summary: Sun shading (hillshade) of a grid: a shaded-relief image lit from the given azimuth and altitude, for visualising topography and enhancing features.
tool.usage:
GRASS-style uses the GRASS r.relief algorithm for softer shading.

For a grid in degrees (geographic), the shading treats the cell size as degrees; the QGIS plugin converts it to metres, so prefer a projected grid.

param.name: in_raster
param.dialogReference: Grid to process (a single-band raster; no-data cells are left as no-data in the result).
param.pythonReference: Grid to process (a single-band raster; no-data cells are left as no-data in the result).

param.name: out_raster
param.dialogReference: Output raster (GeoTIFF), with the input's extent, cell size and coordinate system.
param.pythonReference: Output raster (GeoTIFF), with the input's extent, cell size and coordinate system.

param.name: method
param.dialogReference: Simple: standard hillshade. GRASS-style: the GRASS r.relief algorithm (softer).
param.pythonReference: Simple: standard hillshade. GRASS-style: the GRASS r.relief algorithm (softer).

param.name: altitude
param.dialogReference: Sun altitude above the horizon in degrees (90 = directly overhead).
param.pythonReference: Sun altitude above the horizon in degrees (90 = directly overhead).

param.name: azimuth
param.dialogReference: Sun azimuth in degrees clockwise from north (315 = north-west).
param.pythonReference: Sun azimuth in degrees clockwise from north (315 = north-west).

param.name: z_scale
param.dialogReference: GRASS-style only: vertical exaggeration applied to the grid values.
param.pythonReference: GRASS-style only: vertical exaggeration applied to the grid values.
